trajectory.patch:
The error is a failed assertion `zassert_true(test_event.events == 0x123)` in the `test_event_reset_on_wait` test case. This test validates that when a thread waits for an event with the `reset` flag set, any pre-existing events are cleared before the thread begins waiting.

The failure is caused by a race condition. The main test thread posts an event to `test_event` after signaling the receiver thread to start waiting. It uses `k_yield()` to allow the receiver thread to run. However, `k_yield()` does not guarantee that the receiver thread will execute up to the point where it actually starts waiting on the event object.

If the main thread runs `k_event_post()` before the receiver thread has cleared the event object (as part of `k_event_wait_all` with `reset=true`), the posted event `0x123` is ORed with the existing `0x1234`, resulting in `0x1337`. Then, when the receiver thread does run, it clears the event object to `0` and starts waiting. The wait times out as no new events are posted that satisfy its condition. The final state of `test_event.events` is `0`, causing the assertion `test_event.events == 0x123` to fail.

The fix is to replace `k_yield()` with `k_sleep(DELAY)`. This ensures the receiver thread has enough time to run, call `k_event_wait_all()`, clear the event object, and start waiting before the main thread posts the new event. This synchronization technique is already used in other parts of the same test function.

tests/kernel/events/event_api/src/main.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
	k_yield();           /* Give receiver thread time to run */
========
	k_sleep(DELAY);      /* Give receiver thread time to run */
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
